setup: web/wgsl.html and web/embedder.js, Chrome (Claude desktop browser pane, visible), M1 MacBook Air, Metal, cpu.lock held, 2026-10-21 ~22:00-22:40 EDT. Files from localhost (download excluded). Parity uses each fixture's Python token ids; the JS tokenizer reproduces those ids for every fixture in every package.

parity_cos_min_vs_numpy_reference.note: 6 fixtures per package, 11 to 128 tokens (128 exercises Ettin's local attention window); single sequences and one packed batch of all 6

webgpu_engine.gpu_note: 21 passes in one submit minus 1, /20; ~14-token query
webgpu_engine.end_to_end_note: tokenize + write + dispatch + mapAsync readback, two runs
webgpu_engine.init_note: pipeline compile + aligned weight copy + int8 transpose to [N, K]; range over runs

ort_wasm_fallback.note: single-file model.onnx, graphOptimizationLevel 'all', 1 thread. leaf-ir measured alone on a fresh page: on a page that already ran other onnxruntime sessions it took 116-178 ms even after release(). With the weights in external data onnxruntime-web ran 4x slower (Ettin 37-58 ms), which is why packages ship a single-file model.onnx.
